body:
Fifth sweep: the neuroim2 path, which is the entry point a real fMRI researcher uses and which no reviewer reached. neuroim2 0.19.0 is installed and the adapter has its own test file, so this was not unexercised - but nothing had run the FULL round trip from mask to brain map.

THE ENGINE WORKS ON REAL DATA. 8x8x4 volume, 120 active voxels, spacing 3x3x4. neuroim2_volume_domain preserved all 120 features, neuroim2_searchlights produced 120 rows at mean support 11.1, and relation, geometry and contrast all ran first try. No numerical trouble anywhere.

THE JOURNEY IS BROKEN AT BOTH ENDS - bd-01KZYPC2TDB85HXP6KRABDXFQY.

  GOING IN. The two searchlight constructors return different KINDS of object:

    searchlights(6)                          -> effect_frame_spec   needs compile_frame()
    neuroim2_searchlights(mask, 6, domain)   -> effect_frame        already compiled

  Every example in the documentation drills the pattern compile_frame(searchlights(r), domain).
  A user moving to real data writes the analogue and gets 'specification must be a valid
  additive frame specification'. The correct move is to pass it straight to at=, and nothing
  says so. The asymmetry is probably deliberate - the helper has the mask, so it can compile
  immediately - but it breaks the one pattern the docs teach.

  COMING OUT. as_neurovol() rejects every view object the package produces:

    as_neurovol(contrast_view, mask)        -> values must provide one finite number per
                                               compact domain feature
    as_neurovol(rdm_view, mask)             -> same
    as_neurovol(contrast_view$total, mask)  -> OK, DenseNeuroVol

  The signature is as_neurovol(values, mask, domain, fill, label) and the first argument is a
  bare numeric vector. The user must reach into the view and extract $total before they can
  make a map. This is the step README:379-381 advertises as the way back into brain space,
  and bd-01KZYARD5697TRN2Q3S0E153BM already noted it is demonstrated nowhere. It is now clear
  that a demonstration is not optional polish - without one the call is unguessable, because
  every object the user holds is refused and the message talks about finite numbers per
  feature rather than about what was passed.

  Multi-column views make it worse: an rdm view has one column per condition pair, so there is
  no single vector to extract and no method covers the case.

WHAT THIS SAYS ABOUT THE WHOLE REVIEW, compactly. The path a real fMRI researcher walks is broken at the entrance, broken at the exit, and completely sound in between. Five sweeps now agree on that shape: thirty-three findings, all in the surface, against an engine that is unbiased, exact where it claims to be, invariant across spatial scales, and correct on real volumetric data.

One worked example carrying mask -> domain -> searchlights -> geometry -> contrast -> NeuroVol would have caught both of today's discontinuities, and it is the same example three separate beads have now independently asked for.
